ArchitectureNotes.objective: Provide a GitHub-first, self-contained frontend task knowledge base that an AI agent can extend without catalog or graph drift.
ArchitectureNotes.non-goal: Do not build an executable learning platform, catalog generator, or mandatory repository runtime.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-1: Task metadata is canonical while the student catalog and knowledge graph are derived, so all three artifacts must change atomically.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-2: Structural verification cannot prove solution correctness; mentor content review remains a required gate.
ArchitectureNotes.risk-3: Collapsed details prevent accidental spoilers but do not conceal solutions from raw Markdown or repository search.

contract.purpose: Define the repository's authoring, delivery, synchronization, verification, and stop-condition rules.

export-authoringRules.PURPOSE: Expose task authoring, delivery, tool-resolution, and synchronization requirements

export-verificationContracts.PURPOSE: Expose module, flow, and phase completion evidence

observability.evidence-anchor: M-GOVERNANCE / V-M-GOVERNANCE / XML roots and cross-references
observability.critical-check: All shared artifacts are valid and mutually consistent.

notes.note-1: The approved content architecture is recorded; this module remains partial until written-spec review closes Phase 1 and project-facing governance updates are implemented.

observability.critical-check: All details blocks are closed by default and each hint has its own block.

notes.note-1: The template may contain fenced examples but introduces no runnable repository tooling.

contract.purpose: Store self-contained task cards whose metadata is canonical for every derived navigation artifact.

type-TaskMetadataSet.PURPOSE: Collection of canonical task metadata records exposed to the catalog

export-taskCard.PURPOSE: Expose the complete student-facing exercise through GitHub

observability.evidence-anchor: task slug; metadata values; prerequisite links; asset links; mentor-review status
observability.critical-check: The task is self-contained and every referenced repository path resolves.

notes.note-1: A slug is stable. Renaming it is a migration that must verify every inbound reference.
notes.note-2: Collapsed solutions are spoiler-resistant, not access-controlled.
notes.note-3: The Beads issue remains open until mentor solution review is recorded.
notes.note-4: Each accepted task adds one export-<task-slug> public annotation under M-TASK-LIBRARY in the knowledge graph.

contract.purpose: Provide the GitHub repository entry point and a compact, agent-synchronized projection of task metadata.

export-studentIndex.PURPOSE: Expose one compact canonical table in which every task appears once with all required metadata

observability.evidence-anchor: catalog row; relative task link; projected metadata; unique task slug
observability.critical-check: Every task appears exactly once and matches its canonical metadata.

notes.note-1: The catalog is maintained by an AI agent under contract, not generated by a script.
notes.note-2: The catalog accepts an empty TaskMetadataSet so Phase 3 can create an explicit empty state before the first Phase 4 task wave.

DF-ADD-TASK.NAME: AddTask
DF-ADD-TASK.TRIGGER: Mentor asks an AI agent to add a task
DF-ADD-TASK.step-1: The agent reads M-GOVERNANCE and M-TASK-TEMPLATE.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-2: The agent resolves mandatory metadata and stops if classification is ambiguous.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-3: The agent creates tasks/<task-slug>/README.md and optional colocated assets.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-4: The agent synchronizes README.md and adds one export-<task-slug> annotation to M-TASK-LIBRARY in docs/knowledge-graph.xml.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-5: The agent runs V-M-TASK-LIBRARY, V-M-CATALOG, and V-M-GOVERNANCE checks.
DF-ADD-TASK.step-6: The mentor reviews solution correctness before content acceptance.
DF-ADD-TASK.evidence: Task path, catalog row, graph entry, link-resolution results, document anchors, and mentor-review status.

DF-STUDY-TASK.NAME: StudyTask
DF-STUDY-TASK.TRIGGER: Student opens the repository on GitHub
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-1: The student chooses a task from README.md using visible metadata.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-2: GitHub follows a relative link to the task card.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-3: The student reads the visible goal, prompt, starter code, and readiness criteria.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-4: The student optionally opens theory and then reveals hints one at a time.
DF-STUDY-TASK.step-5: The student opens the solution after attempting the task and completes self-check questions.
DF-STUDY-TASK.evidence: Working relative link, matching metadata, visible required sections, and closed progressive-disclosure blocks.

DF-UPDATE-TASK.NAME: UpdateTask
DF-UPDATE-TASK.TRIGGER: Agent changes task content, metadata, path, prerequisites, or assets
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-1: The agent treats the task card metadata and stable slug as the current canonical record.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-2: The agent updates the task content and identifies every derived artifact and inbound reference.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-3: The agent synchronizes catalog placement and knowledge-graph facts.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-4: The agent checks uniqueness, metadata equality, prerequisites, assets, and relative links.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.step-5: A slug change uses a dedicated migration path and verifies all inbound references.
DF-UPDATE-TASK.evidence: Before/after metadata, unique catalog projection, resolved links, graph delta, and migration evidence when applicable.

Phase-1.name: Governance
Phase-1.goal: Record approved requirements, technology boundaries, module contracts, data flows, verification references, and stop conditions.
Phase-1.step-1: Finalize and review all GRACE planning artifacts.

Phase-2.name: TaskContract
Phase-2.goal: Create the canonical GitHub-first task structure before any task content is added.

Phase-3.name: StudentEntryPoint
Phase-3.goal: Create an understandable repository landing page and an explicit empty catalog state.
Phase-3.step-1: Create README.md with navigation rules and the catalog projection contract.

Phase-4.name: TaskWaves
Phase-4.goal: Add mentor-approved tasks through atomic task, catalog, graph, and evidence updates.
Phase-4.step-1: Add one task card from the canonical template.
Phase-4.step-2: Synchronize the student catalog for the task wave.
Phase-4.step-3: Apply graph and verification deltas and record mentor-review status in the Beads issue.

Phase-5.name: ScaleReview
Phase-5.goal: Reassess controlled vocabularies and deterministic validation only after observed catalog size or drift justifies added tooling.
Phase-5.step-1: Review drift evidence and explicitly approve or reject automation.

ExecutionPolicy.controller-owns: docs/development-plan.xml, docs/knowledge-graph.xml, docs/verification-plan.xml, and catalog synchronization decisions
ExecutionPolicy.worker-owns: Only the explicitly approved task card, colocated assets, and packet-scoped derived updates
ExecutionPolicy.replan-trigger: Ambiguous metadata, missing prerequisite or asset, unexpected GitHub rendering, contradictory task and catalog facts, unreviewed solution logic, or any requirement for new runtime tooling.
ExecutionPolicy.checkpoint-requirement: Every step must leave assumptions, artifacts changed, checks run, observed evidence, mentor-review status, and next action.
